title: I Printed the Apartment Sublet Clause for the Guest Who Never Left

parts.text: I came home at 10:18 p.m. and Priya's cousin was still on the couch with a third suitcase. The lease said guests past fourteen nights were sublets needing written okay. Night fifteen had a date. I was twenty-seven, named on the lease, holding Thai takeout for two that had become three for two weeks. Priya said family was not a sublet. I printed clause 7.4 and left it on the coffee table with a calendar. The cousin asked if I was serious. I was. At 10:31 the landlord's portal pinged because I had also uploaded the calendar as a question, not a complaint, which is how you make portals nervous.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The landlord portal just asked whether unit 3B has an unapproved occupant.

social.video_title: Night fifteen had a clause and a suitcase — Part 1/2
social.description: Thai for three, couch cousin, clause 7.4. The portal woke up. Would you have waited for night thirty?

parts.text: Priya scheduled a departure. The cousin left a spare charger like a flag. I bagged it. The landlord said thank you for asking first. Asking first is a sport. We kept the lease. The couch is a couch again. Family can visit for fourteen nights and a croissant. Night fifteen needs paper. I eat Thai for two. The calendar is blank on purpose.

social.video_title: The spare charger left like a flag — Part 2/2
social.description: Scheduled departure, asked-first portal, Thai for two. Was family a sublet? The clause said the nights did.
